Measuring Line
MEZH-ur-ing line
noun
From measure and line; a cord or surveyor’s line stretched out to mark off and measure land or a building.

Biblical Definition

A measuring line is the surveyor’s cord, stretched out to mark off bounds, measure a wall, or lay out a city, an instrument of ordered apportionment and exact design. In Zechariah the prophet sees “a man with a measuring line in his hand” going forth to measure Jerusalem, to see what is the breadth thereof and the length thereof (Zec 2:1–2), a vision of the city’s restoration, so peopled and blessed that it shall be inhabited as towns without walls. Jeremiah promises that the rebuilt city shall extend by the measuring line: “the measuring line shall yet go forth over against it upon the hill Gareb” (Jer 31:39), every cubit consecrated holy unto the LORD. In Ezekiel’s vision of the temple a man stands with “a line of flax in his hand, and a measuring reed” to lay out the house of God with exactness (Eze 40:3). And the LORD Himself challenges Job, asking who laid the measures of the earth and “who hath stretched the line upon it” (Job 38:5), for the Maker measured out creation with perfect design. The measuring line thus teaches the deliberate, ordered, and gracious purpose of God, who measures out the bounds of His people’s habitation, lays the dimensions of His house, and apportions to His own a goodly heritage. The line that surveys for judgment in some places here surveys for blessing, marking off what God will build and bless.

Webster 1828 Definition

A surveyor’s cord for measuring land or building; in the prophets a figure of God’s ordered purpose to build and bless.

expand to see more

MEASURING LINE, a cord stretched out to measure land or a building.

It marks off bounds and lays out a city with order.

A man measures Jerusalem with a measuring line (Zec 2:1–2).

The line lays out the dimensions of God’s temple (Eze 40:3).

God stretched the line upon the earth at creation (Job 38:5).

Key Scripture

Zec 2:1 — "I lifted up mine eyes again, and looked, and behold a man with a measuring line in his hand."

Zec 2:2 — "Then said I, Whither goest thou? And he said unto me, To measure Jerusalem, to see what is the breadth thereof, and what is the length thereof."

Jer 31:39 — "And the measuring line shall yet go forth over against it upon the hill Gareb, and shall compass about to Goath."

Job 38:5 — "Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it?"

Modern Corruption

A figure of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses the ordered and gracious purpose of God to build and bless His people.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The lesson to recover is the deliberate and ordered purpose of God, who does nothing by chance but measures all by design. The man with the measuring line goes forth to lay out Jerusalem; the line of flax surveys the temple; the LORD Himself stretched the line upon the earth at its founding. God is not a God of confusion but of order, and He measures out the bounds of His people’s habitation and the dimensions of His house with a wisdom that misses nothing.

Where the plumbline tries a wall for judgment, the measuring line here often surveys for blessing, marking off what God will build and inhabit. The vision of Zechariah promises a Jerusalem so blessed it overflows its walls; Jeremiah promises a city whose every measured cubit is holy unto the LORD. So the saint may rest in the truth that the lines are fallen unto him in pleasant places, for the same God who measured creation apportions to His own a goodly heritage, and surveys with grace the place He has prepared to build and to bless.

Hebrew Roots

The phrase joins measure and line, naming the surveyor’s cord that marks off and apportions.

Measure — to mark off by exact extent.

Line — a cord stretched out to survey.

Together: the surveyor’s cord that lays out land or building.

A man measures Jerusalem with a measuring line in Zechariah.

God stretched the line upon the earth at creation.

Usage

"Like a measuring line, God measures out the bounds of His people’s habitation with ordered design."

"The measuring line teaches that God is not a God of confusion but of purposeful order."

"The line that surveys Jerusalem for blessing shows the goodly heritage God apportions His own."
